## Introduction

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(rstanarm)

# Load data
data("df_gaussian", package = "projpred")
dat_gauss <- data.frame(y = df_gaussian$y, df_gaussian$x)

```

```{r}
#| label: prep_prior
#| include: false

# Number of regression coefficients:
( D <- sum(grepl("^X", names(dat_gauss))) )

# Prior guess for the number of relevant (i.e., non-zero) regression coefficients:
p0 <- 5

# Number of observations:
N <- nrow(dat_gauss)

# Hyperprior scale for tau, the global shrinkage parameter (note that for the Gaussian family, 'rstanarm' will automatically scale this by the residual standard deviation):
tau0 <- p0 / (D - p0) * 1 / sqrt(N)
```

*Projection predictive variable selection* (projpred) is a predictive model selection method.

Two steps [@piironen2020, p. 2156]:

1. **Reference model**: "*Construct the best predictive model you can*"
2. **Minimal subset**: "*Find a simpler model that gives similar predictions as the reference model*"

**Projection** [@mclatchie2025]: "*we fit smaller models to the fit of the reference model*"

## Setup

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

This document follows the vignette about the `projpred` package. See: [projpred: Projection predictive feature selection](https://mc-stan.org/projpred/articles/projpred.html).

:::

::: {.column}

For the first part, only `rstanarm` is needed. Load using:

```r
library(rstanarm)
```

Ensure that you set the hyperprior scale for tau (i.e., here `tau0`)

:::

:::

## Fit a reference model

Fit a Bayesian reference model using parallel processing.

```{r}
#| label: fit_reference_mod
#| cache: true

# Set this manually if desired:
ncores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)
options(mc.cores = ncores)

set.seed(50780)

# Fit reference model
refm_fit <- stan_glm(
  y ~ .,
  family = gaussian(),
  data = dat_gauss,
  prior = hs(global_scale = tau0),
  chains = 2, iter = 1000,
  refresh = 0
) |> suppressMessages()
```

## Projpred

Now, load the `projpred` package by:

```{r}
#| label: load_projpred

# Load projpred package
library(projpred)
```

## Search result

Now, you create a reference model object with `get_refmodel` and perform a search through the model space.

```{r}
#| label: ref_model_obj

refm_obj <- get_refmodel(refm_fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: final_model

# Refit the reference model K times:
cv_fits <- run_cvfun(
  refm_obj,
  K = 5
)

# Final cv_varsel() run:
cvvs <- cv_varsel(
  refm_obj,
  cv_method = "kfold",
  cvfits = cv_fits,
  method = "L1",
  nclusters_pred = 20,
  nterms_max = 9,          # determined in preliminary results
  parallel = FALSE,
  verbose = 0 
)

```

## Plot summary

```{r}
#| label: final_model_plot
#| echo: false

options(projpred.plot_vsel_size_position = "primary_x_bottom")
options(projpred.plot_vsel_text_angle = 0)
options(projpred.plot_vsel_show_cv_proportions = TRUE)

plot(
  cvvs, 
  stats = "mlpd", 
  deltas = TRUE   # performance statistics are plotted on difference scale (differences from the BL model)
  )
```

## Table summary

```{r}
#| label: final_model_table
#| echo: false

smmry <- summary(
  cvvs,
  stats = "mlpd",  # performance metric
  type = c("mean", "lower", "upper"),
  deltas = TRUE
  )

```

```{r}
#| label: interactive_table
#| echo: false

# Use package DT for interactive tables
library(DT)

smmry$perf_sub |> 
    datatable(options = list(pageLength = 25, digits = 3)) |> 
    formatRound(columns = names(smmry$perf_sub)[sapply(smmry$perf_sub, is.numeric)], digits = 3)
```

## The math {#sec-math}

@piironen2020 (p. 2166) states that the discrepancy between the induced predictive distribution is defined as

$$
\begin{align}
\mathrm{KL}\big(p(\tilde{y}\mid\mathcal{D}) \,\|\, q(\tilde{y})\big)
&= \mathrm{E}_{\tilde{y}}\big(\log p(\tilde{y}\mid\mathcal{D}) - \log q(\tilde{y})\big) \nonumber \\
&= -\mathrm{E}_{\tilde{y}}\big(\log q(\tilde{y})\big) + \text{const.} \nonumber \\
&= -\mathrm{E}_{\tilde{y}}\big(\log \mathrm{E}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\big(p(\tilde{y}\mid\boldsymbol{\theta})\big)\big) + \text{const.} \nonumber \\
&= -\mathrm{E}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}_*}\Big(\mathrm{E}_{\tilde{y}\mid\boldsymbol{\theta}_*}\big(\log \mathrm{E}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\big(p(\tilde{y}\mid\boldsymbol{\theta})\big)\big)\Big) + \text{const, }
\end{align}
$$

although projection using *pointwise mapping* is used more often in practice.
